maria: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a multimodal synthetic traffic generator to better reproduce the weird tail behavior we've been seeing in staging. The idea is to mix several traffic modes (steady Poisson background, periodic microbursts, long sessions with heavy tail lengths) and explicitly model KV cache cold/miss cascades so kernel selection and batching heuristics flip under load. Wanted to float the approach.
dan: Nice. Can you clarify what "multimodal" means here? Are you mixing request size distributions, or time patterns, or both? :thinking:
maria: Both. Time patterns (Poisson + scheduled spikes + correlated user sessions) and request shapes (short prompts, long multi-turn sessions, and occasional long-generation outliers). We also want to model sequences that grow mid-stream so KV cache warming/eviction interacts with batching. That triggers different kernel paths in the runtime.
kevin: Love that. Two quick requests: (1) seed control so we can reproduce exact runs for apples-to-apples; (2) a knob to toggle "kv-miss-cascade" probability so we can calibrate against production.
maria: Yep — seed control is mandatory. Also adding a "kv_cascade_factor" in the config. Example snippet: ```json
{
  "seed": 314159,
  "modes": [
    {"type": "poisson", "qps": 250, "lambda_ms": 4},
    {"type": "microburst", "burst_qps": 2500, "duration_ms": 120, "period_s": 300},
    {"type": "session", "session_rate": 8, "length_dist": "zipf(1.2, min=1, max=50)"}
  ],
  "kv_cascade_factor": 0.02,
  "sequence_growth_prob": 0.03
}
```
priya: How do you plan to ensure an apples-to-apples comparison vs the old generator? We need identical warmup, same model checkpoint, pinned kernel flags, and identical batching windows.
maria: Good point. Plan: (1) deterministic seed, (2) explicit warmup phase that primes KV entries for X% of user sessions (configurable), (3) we inject a kernel-override flag in the harness so we can force "baseline" vs "opt" kernel selection paths for direct comparison. Also we'll record batch-size histograms.
alex: For metrics: capture p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 latencies, batch size CDF, KV hit/miss ratio over time, kernel-path counters (e.g., aten_small_kernel, fused_attn, int8_path), and a per-request tag for "triggered_eviction".
kevin: Could we also capture per-batch composition (session vs single-shot) so we can see how batching heuristics bias mixing?
perf-bot: Reminder: add trace IDs in the payload so perf tracing correlates request -> kernel selection -> GPU timeline.
maria: Yes, adding trace_id and a lightweight protobuf header. Also adding a small in-harness profiler snapshot: ```
# simple perf dump for a sample surge run
cycles: 1.23e9
peak-batch-size: 64
avg-batch-size: 12.4
kv-miss-rate: 0.067
attn-kernel-swapped: 1142
int8-path-entries: 688
mean-latency-ms: 38.9
99.9-latency-ms: 782.4
```
dan: That 99.9 looks scary — is that from the microburst tails?
maria: Yeah those are bursts combined with session expansion mid-generation causing cache thrash and bigger batches queuing on the CPU side. We want the generator to be able to reproduce that so we can test fallback strategies (e.g., force smaller batching window for sessions or preferential routing to faster kernels).
priya: On evaluation methodology: we should run X repeats per config (n=5), record confidence intervals, and compare only after identical warmups. Also tag commits and model versions in the run metadata.
kevin: For KV modeling: can we replay a small sample of production key-access traces in the generator? Not full PII, but an anonymized frequency table to mimic hotspot keys.
maria: Yes — plan to support "trace-replay mode" where we feed an anonymized histogram of key popularity. That plus a synthetic Zipf session length gives realistic eviction patterns.
alex: One more nit: ensure the generator can vary the batching policy parameter at runtime (max_delay_ms, max_batch_tokens) so we can sweep and measure cost vs p99 tradeoffs.
maria: Agreed. I'll add a sweep harness that submits identical seed + trace with different batching params and emits an apples-to-apples CSV. Example command: `./loadgen --config multimodal.json --batch-window 8 --seed 314159 --out results/batch-8.csv`
kevin: What's the baseline for "apples-to-apples" metrics? CPU/GPU clocks pinned? same CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES?
priya: We should pin hardware, container image, CUDA/Torch versions, and disable background daemons. We'll record env in the run artifact.
perf-bot: New test run scheduled: run_id=mm-2026-03-18-01, seeds=[314159,271828,161803], mode=sweep, estimated runtime=2h.
maria: OK I've pushed the initial generator proto to the repo and a basic config. Next steps: (1) kevin — can you produce an anonymized key-popularity histogram from staging logs? (2) priya — help define the warmup % to match production 95th percentile hit rates. (3) alex — can you add kernel counters into the runtime metrics API?
kevin: On it. I'll post the histogram later today.
priya: I'll run a small profiler to estimate warmup ratio and propose values.
alex: Will add kernel counters, ETA tomorrow.
maria: Thanks all. Once we have the histogram + kernel counters we can run a first apples-to-apples comparison and hopefully reproduce the p99/p999 regression we saw last week. :rocket:
